Scope: Static publisher-page, version, licensing, dependency and sensitive-data review of MiTeC Mail Viewer, E-mail History Browser, Internet History Browser and Instant Messaging History Browser; no payload executed and no personal data opened

MailViewer.PublishedBehavior: Reads Outlook Express 4/5/6 IDX/MBX/DBX databases, Windows Mail/Windows Live Mail and Thunderbird databases, and standalone EML. Displays messages and properties with detailed view, HTML preview, search/filter, address extraction, EML saving, attachment extraction and printing.
MailViewer.CurrentPageLicense: Free for private, educational and non-commercial purposes.
MailViewer.VersionObservation: Current page exposes no release number. Frozen inventory records FileVersion 2.5.1.0 and ProductVersion 2.0.0.0 for MailView.exe.
MailViewer.OperatingSystems: Current page lists Windows XP-11 and Windows Server 2003-2025; this is publisher page support only, not RIDE acceptance.

EmailHistoryBrowser.PublishedBehavior: Collects and filters communication history from Outlook Express, Windows Mail, Windows Live Mail and Thunderbird. The page says message bodies and attachments are excluded; communication metadata remains visible. Portable; current page lists target platforms only through Windows 10.
EmailHistoryBrowser.CurrentPageLicense: Free for private and commercial users. This conflicts with the support EULA's general statement that trial or unregistered freeware is non-commercial; obtain product-specific written clarification before relying on commercial use or redistribution.
EmailHistoryBrowser.VersionObservation: Current page exposes no release number. Frozen inventory records page version 1.2.0 and EHB.exe FileVersion 1.2.0.0/ProductVersion 1.0.0.0.

InternetHistoryBrowser.PublishedBehavior: Portable history viewer that collects visit URLs, dates, times and browser identity. Publisher lists Edge, Internet Explorer, Chrome, Opera, Safari, Firefox, SeaMonkey, Vivaldi, Yandex, Pale Moon and Brave; current listed Windows targets end at Windows 10 and Server 2019.
InternetHistoryBrowser.CurrentPageLicense: Free for private, educational and non-commercial purposes.
InternetHistoryBrowser.VersionObservation: Current page exposes no release number. Frozen inventory records page version 2.5.0; IHB.exe reports FileVersion 2.5.0.0/ProductVersion 2.0.0.0.
InternetHistoryBrowser.DependencyObservation: Frozen archive contains renamed IHB.dll with SQLite Development Team metadata and version 3.35.5. Upstream SQLite public-domain status does not establish exact binary provenance or rights to the surrounding product.

InstantMessagingHistoryBrowser.PublishedBehavior: Portable history viewer that can expose chats, calls and file transfers (when supported by the client), grouped by person or time. Listed clients are Skype, ICQ 7, Windows Live Messenger and Yahoo Messenger; current listed Windows targets end at Windows 10.
InstantMessagingHistoryBrowser.CurrentPageLicense: Free for private and commercial users. This conflicts with the support EULA's general statement that trial or unregistered freeware is non-commercial; obtain product-specific written clarification before relying on commercial use or redistribution.
InstantMessagingHistoryBrowser.VersionObservation: Current page exposes no release number. Frozen inventory records page version 1.2.1 and IMHB.exe FileVersion 1.2.1.0/ProductVersion 1.0.0.0.
InstantMessagingHistoryBrowser.DependencyObservation: Frozen archive contains renamed IMHB.dll with SQLite Development Team metadata and version 3.8.10.2. Upstream SQLite public-domain status does not establish exact binary provenance or rights to the surrounding product.

TermsPage.Observation: The general software EULA says trial or unregistered versions are freeware for non-commercial usage. It also prohibits reverse engineering and separation of the software product. Product-page license wording must be reconciled with this general text for EHB/IMHB and local use/distribution.

ReviewFindings: All four retained archive hashes and the executable/dependency member hashes match the frozen inventory. The inventory records historical/current status and page-version observations; current EHB/IHB/IMHB pages omit a release number, so no fresh publisher release is inferred.

Mail Viewer can reveal message content, addresses and attachments and can save, extract or print them. EHB exposes communication metadata even though it omits bodies and attachments. IHB exposes visited URLs with timestamps and browser identity. IMHB exposes private chats, calls and transfers where supported.

EHB and IMHB product-page claims of free commercial use conflict with the general support EULA's non-commercial unregistered-use statement. Keep commercial use and redistribution unresolved pending product-specific terms; no local entitlement is inferred.

IHB and IMHB bundle renamed SQLite binaries. Static vendor/version metadata and SQLite's public-domain notice do not prove binary provenance, build configuration or redistribution coverage for these artifacts.

MigrationDisposition.Resolved: Pinned artifact versions, publisher-described data surfaces, published OS lists, page license wording and SQLite metadata are recorded.
MigrationDisposition.Partial: Commercial-use and redistribution wording for EHB/IMHB, local entitlement, SQLite provenance, current target support, persistence/output behavior, user-interface behavior and activation remain unverified.
Deferred: Do not open any real mailbox, message, attachment, browser history, chat, call, transfer, profile or account.
Any later behavior check must use isolated synthetic mail stores, browser history and message databases; verify no source mutation, output ownership and cleanup.
Do not promote Windows 11 or Server support from current publisher pages where the listed targets end at Windows 10 or Server 2019; separate RIDE acceptance is required.
Resolve EHB/IMHB commercial-use and distribution terms with the publisher or owner before packaging or relying on commercial use.
MigrationDisposition.EstimateReason: Four product behaviors and sensitive data boundaries are clearer, but no legacy outcome was accepted, retired or excluded; target, license, dependency, persistence and runtime gates remain. Rounded ranges are unchanged.
